y: On forms and at work, say contact number.
a: Or just: what's your number?
e: My contact number is on the card.
m: CONTACT number = how to reach you
q: Contact number is the natural phrase.
s: Save this for your next form.

w: I'll pay at the self-service cashier.
y: The machine where you scan and pay is a self-checkout.
a: Checkout means the place where you pay!
e: I used the self-checkout at the store.
q: The machine is called a self-checkout.
s: Save this for your next shopping trip.

y: Words ending in -ity: stress just before it.
a: Same with university and activity!
e: The electricity went off last night.
We pay for electricity every month.
q: Where is the stress in electricity?
s: Save this and say it out loud.

y: Long for means want very much.
a: It's a strong, poetic word for missing something!
e: She longs for a quiet weekend.
q: After a long winter, I long ___ summer.
Long takes for before a noun.
s: Send this to someone far from home.

y: After hate, use -ing or to plus verb.
a: Love and like work the same way!
s: Tag a friend who hates mornings.

w: He pointed to me with his finger.
y: Point at means show with your finger.
a: In many places, pointing at people feels rude!
q: Point at means show with a finger.
s: Send this to a friend who points.

w: I take 30 minutes to go to school.
r: It takes me 30 minutes to go to school.
y: For time, start with It takes.
a: It takes two to talk!
e: It takes ten minutes to walk there.
q: ___ me an hour to cook dinner.
s: Save this for your next speaking test.

y: A trip is one visit. Travel is the general idea.
a: Travel is usually a verb: I love to travel!
e: We took a trip to the beach.
s: Save this for your next holiday.

w: Can I have a free test?
r: Can I try a free sample?
y: A small free amount to try is a free sample.
a: Shops give samples so you buy more!
e: They gave out free samples of coffee.
Can I have a free sample of this cream?
q: The store gave us a free ___ of cheese.
A small free amount is a sample.
s: Save this for your next shopping trip.

w: I travel to my office by bus.
r: I go to work by bus.
y: For short daily trips, go sounds more natural.
a: Commute is the word for daily work trips!
e: We love to travel in summer.
I commute to work by bus.
m: far away = TRAVEL, every day = GO
q: Every day I ___ to school by bike.
For daily short moves, use go.
s: Save this and share it with a friend.

y: The stress is on the first part.
a: It sounds like KWAN-tuh-tee!
e: Check the quantity on the list.
We need a large quantity of water.
q: Where is the stress in quantity?
s: Save this for your next order.

w: This app is useful to learning.
r: This app is useful for learning.
y: Useful for plus noun or -ing.
a: But: it's useful to know this, with it!
e: This tool is useful for work.
A map is useful for travel.
q: Useful takes for before a noun.
s: Save this. It's useful for you!

w: Can you help me carrying this?
r: Can you help me carry this?
y: Help plus person plus verb. No -ing.
a: Help me to carry is fine too, just less common!
e: She helped me find my keys.
q: Can you help me ___ the box?
Help is followed by a base verb.
s: Save this and help a friend learn it.

w: I will return back to my country.
r: I will go back to my country.
y: Return already means go back. Don't add back.
a: Return back says back two times!
e: When do you go back to school?
Let's go back to the hotel.
s: Send this to a friend who says it.

y: Remind means help someone remember.
a: Your phone reminds you. You remember!
q: Can you ___ me to buy milk?
s: Save this as a reminder!

w: I need to practise every day. (in the US)
r: I need to practice every day.
y: Americans spell practice with C for both noun and verb.
a: British English uses practise with S for the verb!
q: In American English: I ___ piano every day.
American English uses practice for the verb too.
s: Save this and practice it today.

y: It holds your savings, so it ends in -s.
a: Savings is money you keep for later!
e: I put money in my savings account.
q: She opened a ___ account at the bank.
The correct term is savings account.
s: Save this and start saving!

y: Major means big or important, not a boss.
a: In college, your major is your main subject!
q: Traffic is a ___ problem in big cities.
Major means big or serious here.
s: Save this for your next essay.

y: Stress stays on GAR, like in garden.
a: Adding -er doesn't move the stress!
e: My aunt is a great gardener.
q: Where is the stress in gardener?
Stress the first part, as in garden.
s: Save this and say it right.

y: Before spoken or used, say widely.
a: Wide open is fine: the door is wide open!
e: He is widely known as a good teacher.
q: Use widely before a past form.
s: Save this for your next essay.

r: We arranged to meet at six.
y: Arrange to plus verb means make plans.
a: You can also arrange a meeting, with a!
e: I arranged to see the doctor.
q: Arrange is followed by to plus verb.
s: Save this for your next work plan.

w: Where do I register at the hotel?
y: Check in means tell the desk you arrived.
a: At airports you check in too!
e: Check in online to save time.
q: You can ___ online before your flight.
Check in means say you have arrived.
s: Save this for your next trip.

w: I recommend you to visit the museum.
y: Recommend plus -ing, or recommend that you.
a: Recommend that you visit works too!
s: Save this and recommend it to a friend.

y: Invent makes something new. Discover finds it.
a: Nobody invented America. It was always there!
m: new thing = INVENT, hidden thing = DISCOVER
q: Scientists ___ a new kind of fish.
The fish already existed, so we discover it.
s: Send this to a science fan.

y: Hotel cards that open doors are key cards.
a: Phones near key cards can stop them working!
e: I left my key card in the room.
m: card that opens the door = KEY CARD
q: Tap your ___ card to open the door.
s: Save this for your next hotel stay.

w: A: Thanks! B: Anytime? What time?
y: Anytime can mean happy to help again.
a: It's a friendly way to say you're welcome!
s: Save this and use it today.

y: The stress is on the first part.
a: It sounds like SIM-uh-ler!
q: Where is the stress in similar?
s: Save this and say it out loud.

w: I dream to be a doctor.
r: I dream of being a doctor.
y: Dream of plus -ing or noun.
a: Dream about works too, mostly for sleep dreams!
e: She dreams of living in Spain.
I dream of a big house.
s: Send this to a big dreamer.

w: He is thought be very smart.
r: He is thought to be very smart.
y: Is thought to plus verb. Don't drop to.
a: News reports love this form!
e: The house is thought to be old.
She is thought to live in Paris.
q: The castle is thought ___ 500 years old.
Use is thought to plus verb.
s: Save this for your next essay.

w: Sorry, no. The room is full.
r: I'm afraid the room is full.
y: I'm afraid makes bad news softer.
a: It doesn't mean scared here!
s: Save this for your next work call.

y: We always make a mistake.
a: Also make a plan, make a choice!
q: I ___ a mistake on the test.
s: Send this to a friend. No mistakes!

y: You beat people. You win games.
a: You win a prize, but beat a player!
m: WIN the game, BEAT the team
q: We beat a team or a person.
s: Send this to your sports friend.

w: I can't find a car place.
r: I can't find a parking spot.
y: Americans say parking spot or parking space.
a: A parking lot is the whole big area!
e: We found a parking spot near the door.
m: one car = SPOT, many cars = LOT
q: It took ten minutes to find a parking ___.
The common term is parking spot.
s: Save this for your next drive.

w: The phone was a big discovery.
r: The phone was a big invention.
y: A discovery finds something. An invention is new.
a: Fire was a discovery. The lighter was an invention!
e: The discovery of gold changed the town.
q: Finding the new planet was a big ___.
We found it, so it's a discovery.
s: Send this to a science fan.

r: Sunscreen protects you from the sun.
y: Protect someone from danger.
a: Keep and save work the same way: keep from!
e: A helmet protects you from injury.
q: This coat protects me ___ the rain.
s: Save this and protect your English!

r: She taught me how to swim.
y: Teach someone how to do something.
a: Teach me to swim is also correct!
e: He taught me how to cook.
Can you teach me how to drive?
q: My dad taught me ___ ride a bike.
s: Send this to your best teacher.

p: w:i would like to invite you to#phrase
w: I invite you come to my party.
r: I would like to invite you to my party.
y: This polite form works for any invitation.
a: Invite you to plus place or event!
e: I would like to invite you to dinner.
We would like to invite you to our wedding.
q: I would like to invite you ___ our meeting.
s: Save this for your next invitation.

w: They don't allow to smoke here.
y: No person? Allow plus -ing.
a: With a person: allow people to smoke!
e: My boss allowed me to leave early.
q: With no person, use allow plus -ing.
s: Save this for your next trip.

w: A big percent of people agree.
r: A big percentage of people agree.
y: Use percent with a number. Percentage without.
a: Ten percent, but a high percentage!
q: A high ___ of users are young.
s: Save this for your next report.

y: The card that shows your health plan is your insurance card.
a: Clinics almost always ask for it first!
e: Can I see your insurance card?
q: At the clinic, show your ___ card.
s: Save this for your next doctor visit.

w: Let's buy medicine at the spa.
y: A spa is a place for massages and relaxing.
a: A hot tub is sometimes called a spa too!
e: She spent the day at the spa.
s: Save this for your next holiday.

y: Stress the part before -tion: CEP.
a: Same with direction and question!
q: Where is the stress in reception?
s: Save this and say it right.

y: Nearly means almost.
a: Near is about place. Nearly is about almost!
s: Send this to a friend who's nearly late.

w: It's too hot to not drink.
y: Too already means not possible. No extra not.
a: Too hot to drink means you can't drink it!
e: The box is too heavy to carry.
q: Too already gives the no meaning.
s: Save this for your next test.

y: You fill out a form with your details.
a: British speakers often say fill in!
e: I filled out the form online.
s: Save this for your next form.

y: Afraid always takes of.
a: Scared of and frightened of work the same!
s: Send this to a friend who fears spiders.

y: Alone means no people. Lonely means sad.
a: You can be alone and happy!
e: He felt lonely in the new city.
q: I live ___, but I'm not lonely.
s: Send this to someone who lives alone.

w: Put the bottle in the recycle trash.
r: Put the bottle in the recycling bin.
y: The box for paper and plastic is a recycling bin.
a: In the US, people also say can!
e: Don't put food in the recycling bin.
q: Put the cans in the ___ bin.
s: Save this and recycle more!

w: I saw an advertisement of the job.
r: I saw an advertisement for the job.
y: An advertisement for a thing you can buy or get.
a: Most people just say ad!
e: I saw an ad for cheap flights.
q: There's an advertisement ___ a new phone.
s: Save this and share it.
